subject: Biotechnology
title: GMOs on Your Plate
description: One-minute skill: GMOs on Your Plate.

hook.text: Over 90% of US corn, soybeans, and cotton are genetically modified — you eat GMOs almost every day.

buildup.text: Bt crops carry a bacterial gene that produces insect-killing protein — reducing pesticide spraying.

discovery.text: Roundup Ready crops tolerate herbicide — farmers spray weeds without harming the crop itself.

twist.text: Weeds evolved resistance to Roundup — the biotech solution created an evolutionary arms race.

climax.text: Golden Rice adds vitamin A to prevent blindness — yet regulatory battles delayed it for over 20 years.

punchline.text: GMOs feed billions — the debate is about trust, not just science.

quiz.question: What does Bt crop technology do?
options: Makes crops grow faster using growth hormones
Produces an insect-killing protein from a bacterial gene, reducing pesticide use
Changes the color of crops to repel birds

details.summary: Genetically modified organisms in agriculture have genes added or modified to confer traits like insect resistance, herbicide tolerance, or improved nutrition. Over 190 million hectares of GMO crops are grown globally, primarily soy, corn, cotton, and canola.
details.whyItMatters: GMOs are among biotechnology's most widespread and debated applications. Scientific consensus supports their safety while public perception remains divided, making GMO literacy essential for informed agricultural and food policy discussions.
takeaways: GMO crops carry inserted or modified genes for desired agricultural traits
Over 190 million hectares of GMO crops are planted globally each year
Major scientific organizations confirm the safety of approved GMO foods

faq.question: Are GMO foods safe to eat according to scientific evidence?
faq.answer: Yes. Every major scientific organization worldwide, including the WHO, the National Academies of Sciences, and the EU Commission, has concluded that approved GMO foods are as safe as conventional counterparts. Thousands of studies over decades support this consensus.

faq.question: What are the main concerns about GMO crops?
faq.answer: Environmental concerns include gene flow to wild relatives and herbicide resistance in weeds. Socioeconomic issues involve corporate seed control and farmer dependency. Ecological concerns include impacts on non-target organisms. Each requires case-by-case assessment.
